intended_object: For a profinite group G and a family (S_U) of subgroups S_U ≤ G/U, one for each open normal subgroup U, the closed subgroup ⋂_U π_U⁻¹(S_U) of G. When the family is compatible, this is the inverse limit lim S_U inside G ≅ lim G/U, and it is the unique closed subgroup whose image in each G/U is S_U (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Ch. I §1). I took this from the docstring, the module documentation and the theorems that follow it in the file.
explanation:
The body uses `reconstruct G S`, which is `⨅ U, (S U).comap (QuotientGroup.mk' U)`. That is exactly the set of g such that, for every open normal U, the class of g in G/U lies in S_U. Closedness is proved correctly: each G/U is discrete because U is open, so each preimage is closed, and an intersection of closed sets is closed.

The definition does not assume the family is compatible. That is harmless: the intersection is a closed subgroup for any family. Compatibility is only needed in the later theorems (`map_reconstruct`, `closedReconstruction_unique`), and `closedReconstruction_images` shows that the construction inverts L ↦ (images of L).

On generality: the intersection itself would make sense in any topological group. But the purpose of the construction is the correspondence between closed subgroups and compatible families of subgroups of the finite quotients. That correspondence is a statement about profinite groups, since it needs compactness and the fact that the open normal subgroups form a neighbourhood basis of 1. So the profinite setting is the natural one.

I found no Mathlib declaration that builds a closed subgroup from such a family of quotient subgroups.
